Finansal Farkındalık: An element that supports persons behaving more rationally in their decision-making processes by increasing their knowledge of, and level of awareness regarding, financial risks.
Finansal Hesaplar: A set of accounts showing the financial transactions with one another of all the financial assets and liabilities created, converted into cash and transformed in an economy, by sectors and by financial instruments. Taking as its basis the financial transactions domestic sectors carry out with one another and with the rest of the world, it shows how the surplus or deficit in the capital account is financed with financial assets and liabilities. To access the Financial Accounts
Finansal Hizmetler Anketi - FHA: A survey applied monthly with the aim of monitoring the assessments of the recent past and the forward-looking expectations of the managers of financial institutions in Türkiye regarding their business situation, and producing indicators that will reflect the tendencies and developments in the financial services sector. To access the Financial Services Survey
Finansal Hizmetler Güven Endeksi - FHGE: An indicator, with the aim of following the developments in the financial services sector, in which the answers given to different questions of the Financial Services Survey are evaluated together and summarized. Click to access the Financial Services Confidence Index.
Finansal hizmetlere erişim: The concept describing to what extent economic units can easily benefit from banking and insurance services.
Finansal istikrar: The resilience or protection of financial institutions such as banks and stock exchanges in a country against unexpected changes.
Finansal İstikrar: Refers to the stability and resilience against shocks in the financial markets, in the institutions operating in these markets and in the payment systems. Stability in these areas generally brings with it the healthy and stable functioning of the financial system, and hence the productive allocation of the resources in the economy and the appropriate management and distribution of risks. It is a known fact that financial instability, on the other hand, will create serious problems in the economy, and the high cost of the financial crises experienced points to the importance of financial stability.
Finansal İstikrar Komitesi: The committee established with the change made in Law No. 4059 by Decree-Law No. 637, which entered into force on 8 June 2011, in order to closely and effectively monitor macro financial risks in Türkiye. The Financial Stability Committee, under the chairmanship of the Minister of Treasury and Finance of the Republic of Türkiye, consists of the Governor of the CBRT, the Chairman of the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency, the Chairman of the Capital Markets Board and the President of the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund. Its fundamental duties are to control financial risks by providing coordination among the member institutions and to prevent the formation of systemic risk.
Finansal İstikrar Kurulu: An international organization established in April 2009 as the successor of the Financial Stability Forum, with the aim of coordinating the work of national financial authorities and international standard-setting bodies, and of developing and implementing effective regulation, supervision and other financial sector policies, for the achievement of financial stability.
Finansal Kesim Dışındaki Firmaların Net: In Türkiye, the difference between the foreign currency assets and foreign currency liabilities of firms operating outside the financial sector arising from their transactions with the domestic financial sector and with residents abroad. It is used as an indicator of how much of the real sector's foreign-currency-linked liabilities it can cover with its foreign-currency or foreign-currency-indexed assets. To access the Non-Financial Sector Firms' Net FX Position
Finansal Kiralama: The financing technique used to meet the medium-term funding needs of enterprises. A contract signed between the lessee and the lessor that leaves the ownership of a good selected by the lessee and purchased by the lessor with the lessor, and its use with the lessee.
Finansal Okuryazarlık: The competence of an individual to possess the fundamental financial knowledge enabling effective and conscious decisions in the process of managing one's personal budget, and, by implementing these decisions, to raise individual and social financial welfare.
Finansal Piyasa Altyapılarına İlişkin Pr: The standards prepared for financial market infrastructure institutions, contained in the report published in 2012 by the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures (CPMI), an international standard-setting organization in the field of payments established under the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), and the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO), an international standard-setting organization in the field of securities. Under the said report, financial market infrastructures are payment systems, securities settlement systems, central counterparties, central securities depositories and data repositories.
Finansal serbestleşme: A country's removal of the restrictions on its financial markets and its integration with the outside world in the financial sense.
Firma: The institutions that offer to the market the goods and services demanded by society, with the aim of making profit.
Fisher etkisi: The phenomenon of the nominal interest rate coming out higher than the real interest rate because of the inflation expectation.
Fixed Rebates: Rebates in which there is a single rebate target for buyers and, linked to this target, a single rebate rate is applied.
Fiyat: The payment made in return for a product bought or sold.
Fiyat alıcı: A buyer or seller having no influence whatsoever over the price of a certain product.
Fiyat ayrımcılığı: The practice of selling a certain product to different buyers in ways that earn different amounts of profit.
Fiyat endeksi: A series of numbers measuring the price average of a certain group of products for different periods.
Fiyat esnekliği: Or the price elasticity of demand, in short εP: a basic type of elasticity showing by what percentage the quantity demanded of a product decreases as a result of a one percent increase in its price.
Fiyat istikrarı: The prices of products in a country remaining constant over time, or changing at a low and predictable rate.
Fiyat İstikrarı: Refers to a low and stable inflation rate, directed toward the long-term fundamental aims of monetary policy (growth and employment), to the extent that it will not be effective in the decision-making processes of economic units.
Fiyat kısıtlaması: The market intervention the state implements by determining the lowest or highest price to be paid for a product.
Fiyat liderliği modeli: The oligopoly model in which a dominant firm sets the price and the other small firms comply with it.
Fiyat savaşı: Firms acting with the aim of increasing or preserving market share successively cutting prices in response to one another.
Fiyat yapıcı: A buyer or seller possessing influence over the price of a certain product.
Fiyat-defter değeri oranı: The ratio of market value to book value; below 1 generally indicates low valuation or poor asset quality.
Fiziksel sermaye: The human-made equipment used in production, such as machinery, factories, vehicles and buildings.
Fizyokrasi: The school of thought maintaining that wealth is determined by the amount of agricultural land owned, and that at the basis of economic relations lies a natural order.
Fon: Refers to banknotes, coins, book money or electronic money.
Fonksiyonel gelir dağılımı: The income distribution measure showing how total income is distributed among the production factors.
Fonu: The capital formation established through the partnerships of qualified investors who invest in the technology- and innovation-oriented ventures of medium-sized enterprises with high growth potential. Entrepreneur: the person or persons who see business opportunities in any field, take the possible risks and commit themselves to the business, and ensure its continuity.
Forfaiting: The purchase by a bank or a financial institution specialized in this field of receivables, particularly those arising from the export of goods and services, that can be collected according to a certain payment plan. It is a financing instrument for long-term and credit-based export-import transactions, generally used for investment goods.
Forum Shopping: The case of undertakings submitting their complaints or notifications to all of the different institutions having jurisdiction on the same matter, or to one of the institutions, seeking to ensure that decisions favorable to the undertaking are taken. Undertakings try to take advantage of the conflicts of jurisdiction among the institutions. With the aim of preventing jurisdictional conflicts, protocols can be made among the competent institutions.
Functional Discounts: Discounts given in return for resellers providing certain sales activities and after-sales services.
Fırsat eşitliği: All members of society having equal opportunities in matters such as education, work and health, regardless of differences such as gender, ethnic origin and geographic location.
Fırsat maliyeti: The return forgone by giving up a resource's best alternative use; it forms the basis of the discount rate in capital budgeting.
Fırsatı kaçırma korkusu: The unplanned purchase of a rising asset at a late price, out of fear of missing it; it intensifies in the final segment of speculative bubbles.
Gama: The rate of change of delta with respect to the underlying price (Γ = N′(d1)/(S·σ·√T)); it shows how often the hedge needs to be renewed.
Gayri safi katma değer: Or in short GVA: the total value added created in the economy, or in a certain branch of the economy, in a given period.
Gayri safi milli hasıla: Or in short GNP: the market value of all the final goods and services produced using the resources belonging to a country's citizens in a given period.
Gayri safi sabit sermaye oluşumu: Or in short GFCF: the total of all the fixed capital expenditures made by the economic units resident domestically.
Gayri safi yatırım harcamaları: Or in short I: the main expenditure heading covering the purchases of fixed capital and inventories by the economic units domestically.
Gayri Safi Yurt İçi Hasıla - GSYİH: The value added produced within a country's borders in a given period.
Gayri safi yurtiçi mutluluk: The national income and welfare measure put forward in 1972 by the King of Bhutan, Jigme Singye Wangchuck.
Gayrı Sıhhi Müessese: Defined as workplaces carrying the risk of harming those around them biologically, chemically, physically, psychologically and socially during their activities, or of polluting natural resources.
Gecikmeli Net Mutabakat: A net settlement method in which the settlement is carried out according to the netting principle at the end of a predefined settlement cycle.
Gelir dağılımı: The measure describing how, and to what degree equally, the income produced in a society is distributed among the different segments of that society.
